newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 12.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Banks have decided to off-load their property after realising the bill they will be presented with following the imposition of a tax this year on major real estate holdings. Banks will carry the burden of the new tax as their holdings are estimated at billions of drachmas, many of them passed in at auction.

--Foreigners are fuelling 35 percent of investment in the Greek capital market; the increased interest in recent years is attributed to a trend internationally for gradual expansion, particularly in the constructions sector.
--Final decisions on the buy-out of vintners Cambas A.E. will be taken today at a meeting of creditor banks.
--The national economy ministry's committee of exports is re-examining export policy following changes to the export credits system.

--The estimated six trillion drachmas in the forthcoming "Santer Package" for Greece will go towards infrastructure works such as construction, new technology, telecommunications and financing of major public workers projects such as the Athens Metro, the Egnatia Highway and the Patras-Athens-Thessaloniki highway. The government is feverishly preparing for the final decisions on the levels of financing, to be taken in mid-July.

--The National Mortgage Bank is preparing new and innovative products for the housing credit market as part of its new offensive. Sources say the new products will be ready within the next two months and will include new housing loans modelled on those offered overseas and adjusted for Greek conditions and subsidised lending interest rates.

--Supervisory procedures on Athens Stock Exchange members will change radically with the implementation of the Capital Market Commission's decisions on the liquidity of capital as well as the definition of a new monitoring process.

--A brake on forex lending by business and private customers is being attempted by the government in an effort to stem the tide which threatens the balance of payments and the Greek banking system. The national economy ministry, following consultations with the Bank of Greece, is pushing ahead with a legislative amendment which will see forex lending subjected to higher charges, whether lent by foreign or Greek banks.

--The finance ministry is gearing towards abolishing an "unfortunate" recent provision which taxes donations, saying it is not effectively meeting its original goal of averting tax evasion but is hurting hundreds of charitable institutions.

--The rise and rise of the Athens Stock Exchange since the beginning of the year has brought comparisons of the last money market "spring" of 1990, when the general price index hit a record high, but experts say this year's advance bears little similarity.

--The International Monetary Fund has recommended the privatisation or floating of other public organisations and enterprises (DEKOs) apart from Greece's telecoms organisation OTE and banks as well as stepped up of fund absorption and financing of major public works projects.
